mathematical_scope: Constructs two sampled sums of two gauged Green inverses, multiplies them densely, checks a cut selected for the first sum, and verifies a nonzero Fourier covariance defect. The example demonstrates that the additive cut barrier need not survive a product; it explicitly does not construct Fourier.
input_and_guard_coverage: No n>0/integer guard. n is passed to field_for_root and separation helpers. Dense product assumes square compatible matrices; cut assumes valid indices. Random assertions product_rank>2 and covariance_rank!=0 are seed-specific experimental outcomes, not input-wide guarantees.
cost_and_scaling: Dense q=2 Green matrices use O(N²) storage and column solves. dense_product_mod and covariance rank cost O(N³) modular arithmetic. The returned apply-cost string describes a hypothetical factored application using four O(N) solves, not the cost of product_escape_audit.
test_evidence: Test_phase17 test 20 uses N=32,64 and the default seed. No varying-seed exhaustive search, counterexample fallback, dimension rejection, or full Fourier equality test; covariance nonzero is sufficient to reject the sample.
dependency_identity: Assigned green_sum_cert exact hash 8137aead…; json/random standard library.

findings.finding: The report mixes dense cubic audit execution with an O(N) factored-application description. This distinction must be preserved in any performance summary.
Product escape establishes a limitation of this one additive obstruction, not Fourier synthesis or a universal escape theorem for every seed.

acceptance_boundary: Accept as a designed finite-instance positive control for barrier escape and a Fourier falsification control; not evidence for a fast Fourier transform.
